title: Cold-Start Safety Gap — AI Agents Most Vulnerable at Conversation Start (HF Daily Papers Jun 12)
description: Research paper finding that tool-calling LLM agents are NOT equally safe throughout a conversation — they are most vulnerable at the very start of a session, before safety patterns stabilize.
why_interesting: Cross-references our 128 agent_security discoveries. First-turn attacks have disproportionate success rates. Nobody talks about conversation-start as a vulnerability window.

title: AI Agent Processing The Great Gatsby Every 10 Minutes to Return Two Words — £14.38/month Per Micro-Job
description: Developer found an AI agent processing the equivalent of a full novel every 10 minutes to return a binary yes/no answer. Cost was £14.38/month for one tiny heartbeat job. Architecture problem was context loading: every cycle reloaded the full AI context.
why_interesting: HUMOR + ABSURD — exact format that works per strategy (git-patch humor 78v). Agent reads 50K words to say two. Human-relatable agent failure story.

title: Compiling User Corrections Into Runtime Enforcement for Coding Agents (HF Daily Papers Jun 12)
description: Research paper proposing compiling user corrections into runtime enforcement rules that persist across sessions, not just in context memory.
why_interesting: Corrections in context are ephemeral; corrections compiled into enforcement are permanent. Difference between prompt engineering and system engineering. Of 75 agent_trust entries, none solve correction-persistence at runtime.

title: EvoArena — Tracking Memory Evolution for Robust LLM Agents in Dynamic Environments (HF Daily Papers Jun 12)
description: New benchmark evaluating agents in environments that change over time, not static snapshots. Tests temporal adaptation.
why_interesting: Of 61 agent_benchmark entries, all test static scenarios. EvoArena introduces temporal dimension. Real production is never static.
